scoring_method.3: Your candidate match is your party match, recalculated with the three Surrey-Fleetwood questions counting double. There is no separate candidate score; no evidence exists to build one.
scoring_method.5: Candidate alignment reuses party scores. The three Surrey-Fleetwood questions count double on top of the importance weight; provincial questions count once. Questions without a published party position are left out for that candidate. No candidate-specific adjustment: Brar voted with his party on every recorded vote checked; the challengers have no record or local positions. CentreBC scores follow its October 10 platform.

local.formula: local_alignment(c) = sum over answered questions q of ( w_q * m_q * s_q(party(c)) ) / sum over answered questions q of ( w_q * m_q * 4 ). w_q = importance weight (low 0.5, medium 1, high 2). m_q = 2 if q.scope == 'local' else 1. s_q(P) = scores[P] of the chosen option. Skipped questions are excluded from both sums. Questions where party_positions[party(c)].no_position is true are excluded from both sums for that candidate only (no published position), so denominators differ by candidate. candidate_adjustment = 0 for all five candidates. Family local score = mean of members' local_alignment per candidate.

how_to_vote.voting_day: Saturday, October 24, 2026, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Pacific time.
how_to_vote.advance_voting: Friday October 16 to Wednesday October 21, 2026, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time. Not every location is open every day; check yours.
how_to_vote.mail_in: Request a vote-by-mail package online or by phone (1-800-661-8683) by October 18. Elections BC must receive it by 8 p.m. Pacific time on October 24 for it to be counted. If you are not registered or your voter information is out of date, prove your identity and address by uploading ID to Elections BC's ID upload system or by including photocopies of your ID with the returned package.
how_to_vote.eligibility: Canadian citizen, 18 or older on October 24, 2026, and a BC resident since April 23, 2026.
how_to_vote.id_rules: Prove identity and address one of three ways: (1) one government photo ID with your name and address (BC driver's licence, BCID, BC Services Card with photo, Certificate of Indian Status, or another government card with name, photo and address); (2) two documents with your name, at least one with your current address (electronic accepted, handwritten generally not); (3) someone vouches for you: a registered voter in your electoral district, a spouse, parent, grandparent, adult child, adult grandchild or adult sibling, or a person with authority to make personal care decisions for you. A voucher who is not a relative or personal care authority can vouch for only one voter, and you and the voucher each make a solemn declaration.
how_to_vote.where: Find advance and election-day locations with the voting-place lookup on elections.bc.ca. District electoral offices also take voters until 4 p.m. on October 24. The October 17 municipal election is a separate vote with its own locations.
how_to_vote.other_dates: Municipal elections October 17, 2026. Televised leaders' debate October 14 (Eby, Doerkson, Lowan). Final count November 6 to 10 (planned).
